items.text: A frozen, versioned release corpus covers source, layout, language, quality, length, and action-risk slices.
OCR, structure, field, calibration, false-accept, review, latency, and cost metrics pass declared slice gates.
Schema and normalization changes are versioned, migration-tested, and compatible with declared consumers.
Burst, slow-document, retry, worker-loss, and reviewer-capacity tests keep queue age inside the service objective.
File isolation, tenant boundaries, access, retention, deletion, redaction, and external-processor obligations are approved.
Original bytes, transforms, parser configuration, schema, policy, and candidate versions can be replayed without overwriting history.
The candidate runs in shadow on identical inputs and field-level diffs are reviewed before it receives decision authority.
Canary exposure is bounded by tenant, document family, action, and volume rather than only a global traffic percentage.
Queue age, false accepts, slice regressions, schema failures, and security events have explicit stop and rollback thresholds.
Every release alert names an owner, investigation evidence, safe fallback, affected-record query, and replay runbook.
